resumen: Quién hace, a quién le pasa, de quién es algo y cuándo lo haces tú mismo: I · me · my · mine · myself, el genitivo 's y whose.

teoria.paraQue: Para decir quién hace algo, a quién le pasa, de quién es una cosa y cuándo alguien lo hace por sí mismo: I called her. · That's my desk. · This one is mine. · I did it myself. · It's Laura's idea.
teoria.llave: La llave es la fila de la tabla: cada persona tiene cinco formas y la posición en la frase te dice cuál usar. Delante del verbo, sujeto (I). Detrás del verbo o de una preposición, objeto (me). Delante de un sustantivo, adjetivo posesivo (my). Solo, sin sustantivo, pronombre posesivo (mine). Cuando el sujeto y el objeto son la misma persona, o para decir «yo mismo», reflexivo (myself).

formulas.formula: I · you · he · she · it · we · they + verbo
verbo / preposición + me · you · him · her · it · us · them
my · your · his · her · its · our · their + sustantivo
mine · yours · his · hers · ours · theirs (solo, sin sustantivo)
formulas.ejemplo: That desk is ((mine)). · The idea was ((theirs)).

formulas.formula: myself · yourself · himself · herself · itself · ourselves · yourselves · themselves

reglas: Tabla completa: I–me–my–mine–myself · you–you–your–yours–yourself (plural yourselves) · he–him–his–his–himself · she–her–her–hers–herself · it–it–its–(no hay)–itself · we–us–our–ours–ourselves · they–them–their–theirs–themselves.
El posesivo concuerda con el dueño, no con la cosa: his car (de él), her car (de ella). En español «su» no lo dice; en inglés sí.
Adjetivo posesivo + sustantivo (my book); pronombre posesivo solo (It's mine). Nunca «mine book» ni «my» suelto.
Los posesivos no llevan apóstrofo: its, yours, hers, ours, theirs. Con apóstrofo son contracciones: it's = it is · you're = you are · they're = they are.
Tell, send, give, show y ask aceptan la persona pegada: tell me, send me, show me. Pero explain, say, describe y suggest necesitan «to»: explain it to me, say it to her.
Reflexivo cuando el sujeto y el objeto son la misma persona (I hurt myself, she introduced herself) o para subrayar que lo hizo esa persona (I did it myself). By myself = solo, sin ayuda.
Muchos verbos reflexivos del español no lo son en inglés: I get up, I relax, I concentrate, I feel good (no «I feel myself good»).
Posesión de personas y animales con 's: Laura's desk, my boss's car, the client's feedback. «The desk of Laura» suena raro. Con cosas, of: the end of the month, the name of the campaign.
Plural en -s: solo apóstrofo (my parents' house, the clients' feedback). Plural irregular: 's (the children's room). Dos dueños: el 's va solo en el último (Laura and Mike's office).
Whose = de quién (Whose phone is this?). Who's = who is. Suenan igual, se escriben distinto.
Con dos sujetos, yo va último y en forma de sujeto: Laura and I went (no «me and Laura went»). Detrás de preposición, objeto: between you and me.

usos.uso: Decir de quién es algo en casa
usos.ejemplo: That's ((my)) towel; ((yours)) is the blue one.
((My)) sister and ((her)) husband live near ((my parents')) house.
I {{fixed}} the bike ((myself)). · The kids {{made}} dinner ((themselves)).

usos.uso: Presentar al equipo y repartir tareas
usos.ejemplo: This is Laura, ((our)) account director. ((Her)) team handles the client; ((mine)) handles production.
Could you {{send}} ((me)) the deck and {{explain}} the timeline to ((me))?

usos.uso: Aclarar de quién es la idea o el error
usos.ejemplo: ((Whose)) idea was this? — It was ((Mike's)), but we {{developed}} it ((ourselves)).

errores.porque: Explain necesita «to» delante de la persona: explain something to someone. Es un calco de «explícame».
El posesivo concuerda con el dueño: Laura es mujer → her. En español «sus» no distingue.

errores.mal: The car of my boss is new.
errores.porque: Con personas se usa el genitivo 's, no «of». Es un calco de «el carro de mi jefe».

errores.mal: Is mine book on your desk?
errores.bien: Is my book on your desk?
errores.porque: Delante de un sustantivo va el adjetivo posesivo (my). Mine va solo: Is that book mine?
Its es posesivo y no lleva apóstrofo. It's = it is.

errores.mal: Your right, the deadline is Friday.
errores.bien: You're right, the deadline is Friday.
errores.porque: You're = you are. Your es posesivo: your deadline.

errores.mal: Me and Mike went to the gym.
errores.bien: Mike and I went to the gym.
errores.porque: Como sujeto se usa I, y en inglés yo voy al final: Mike and I.
Los pronombres posesivos nunca llevan apóstrofo: hers, yours, ours, theirs.

contraste.nota: Dueño hombre → his; dueña mujer → her. En español los dos son «su».
Herself: la misma persona. Her: otra persona.

frases.en: Could you explain it to me?

teoria.tip: Mira la posición: delante del verbo → I; detrás → me; delante de un sustantivo → my; sin sustantivo → mine; la misma persona dos veces → myself. Y si dudas entre its / it's, your / you're, whose / who's: si puedes decir «is» o «are», lleva apóstrofo.

palabras.ejemplo: Can you send me the file?

hueco.frase: Can you send ___ the file? (a mí)

palabras.nota: Detrás del verbo o de una preposición: call me, with me, for me.
Siempre delante de un sustantivo: my desk, my team.
Solo, sin sustantivo: It's mine (no «mine coffee»).

palabras.ejemplo: I cut myself while I was cooking.

hueco.frase: I cut ___ while I was cooking. (me, a mí mismo)

palabras.nota: By myself = solo, sin ayuda.

palabras.es: tú, usted, ustedes; te, lo, le
palabras.nota: Sujeto y objeto son iguales: You called. · I called you.
Sin apóstrofo. You're = you are.

palabras.ejemplo: This pen isn't mine; it's yours.
palabras.nota: Sin apóstrofo: yours, nunca «your's».
Plural: yourselves.
Objeto de he: Call him. · Talk to him.

hueco.frase: Andrés lost ___ keys again. (sus, de él)

palabras.nota: His sirve con sustantivo (his car) y sin él (the car is his).
Nunca «hisself».

palabras.es: la, le, a ella; su (de ella)
palabras.ejemplo: I told her about the meeting.

hueco.frase: I told ___ about the meeting. (a ella)

palabras.nota: Her es objeto (call her) y adjetivo posesivo (her desk).

hueco.frase: The red jacket is ___. (suya, de ella)

palabras.nota: Nunca «her's».

palabras.ejemplo: Laura introduced herself to the client.

hueco.frase: Laura introduced ___ to the client. (se presentó ella misma)

palabras.nota: Introduce yourself / herself / ourselves = presentarse.

palabras.es: lo, la (una cosa o animal); ello
palabras.ejemplo: I like the idea. Let's present it tomorrow.

hueco.frase: I like the idea. Let's present ___ tomorrow. (la)

palabras.nota: Sujeto y objeto iguales: It works. · I love it.

palabras.es: su (de una cosa, empresa o animal)
palabras.nota: Sin apóstrofo. It's = it is.

palabras.es: él mismo, ella misma (una cosa); solo
palabras.ejemplo: The app updates itself every night.

hueco.frase: The app updates ___ every night. (se actualiza sola)

palabras.nota: The problem solved itself = se resolvió solo.

palabras.ejemplo: The client sent us the brief.
palabras.nota: Objeto de we: Join us. · Tell us.
Delante de sustantivo: our team, our client.
Sin apóstrofo: ours, nunca «our's».
By ourselves = solos, sin ayuda.

palabras.ejemplo: I'll send them the deck tonight.

hueco.frase: I'll send ___ the deck tonight. (les, a ellos)

palabras.nota: Objeto de they: Call them. · Work with them.

hueco.frase: My parents sold ___ house. (su, de ellos)

palabras.nota: Their = su · there = allí · they're = they are.

palabras.ejemplo: This table is ours and that one is theirs.

hueco.frase: This table is ours and that one is ___. (suya, de ellos)

palabras.nota: Sin apóstrofo: theirs.
Nunca «theirselves».

ejercicios.q: This is ___ laptop. Don't touch it.
ejercicios.explica: Delante de un sustantivo (laptop) va el adjetivo posesivo: my.

ejercicios.q: Laura forgot ___ keys at the gym.
ejercicios.explica: El posesivo concuerda con el dueño: Laura es mujer → her. His sería de un hombre.
Detrás del verbo va el pronombre objeto: send me.

ejercicios.q: Andrés is at the gym. ___ goes every morning.
ejercicios.explica: Delante del verbo va el pronombre sujeto: he goes.
Sin sustantivo detrás va el pronombre posesivo: It's mine (no «it's my»).

ejercicios.q: The dog is hungry. Give ___ some food.
ejercicios.explica: Objeto de it es it: give it some food. Its es posesivo e it's = it is.

ejercicios.q: Mike and I work together. ___ team is small. (our / ours)
ejercicios.explica: Delante de un sustantivo (team) va el adjetivo posesivo: our.

ejercicios.q: This bag isn't ___. It's Camila's. (my / mine)
ejercicios.explica: Sin sustantivo detrás va el pronombre posesivo: mine.

ejercicios.q: I called Sarah last night, but ___ didn't answer. (she / her)
ejercicios.explica: Delante del verbo (didn't answer) va el sujeto: she.

ejercicios.q: The company changed ___ logo last year. (its / it's)
ejercicios.explica: Posesivo sin apóstrofo: its logo. It's = it is.
Delante de un sustantivo va my, no mine ni me.
Detrás del verbo va el objeto me. Myself solo si el sujeto también soy yo.

ejercicios.es: El carro de mi jefe es nuevo.
ejercicios.explica: Con personas se usa el genitivo 's: my boss's car, no «the car of my boss».

correccion: Explain the brief to me, please.
ejercicios.explica: Explain necesita «to» delante de la persona: explain something to someone.

ejercicios.frase: Her name is Laura and she works with us.
ejercicios.explica: Her (posesivo), she (sujeto) y us (objeto) están en la posición correcta. Correcta.
Cinco formas por persona: sujeto, objeto, adjetivo posesivo, pronombre posesivo y reflexivo.

ejercicios.texto: Is this your coffee or mine?
respuestas: Is this your coffee or mine?
ejercicios.explica: Your delante de sustantivo (your coffee); mine solo, sin sustantivo.
Dueño hombre → his. His sirve con sustantivo (his car) y sin él (it's his).

ejercicios.q: The clients sent ___ feedback this morning, and it's not good.
ejercicios.explica: Delante de un sustantivo (feedback) va el adjetivo posesivo: their. They're = they are.

ejercicios.q: Your deck is good, but ___ is clearer.
ejercicios.explica: Sin sustantivo va el pronombre posesivo hers (= her deck). Nunca con apóstrofo.

ejercicios.q: The client's app is popular. ___ new version launches in May.
ejercicios.explica: La app es it → posesivo its, sin apóstrofo. It's = it is.

ejercicios.q: Mike cut ___ while he was cooking. (reflexivo)
ejercicios.explica: El sujeto (Mike) y el objeto son la misma persona: himself.

ejercicios.q: Is this pen ___? I found it on your desk. (your / yours)
ejercicios.explica: Sin sustantivo detrás va el pronombre posesivo: yours.

ejercicios.q: The clients loved the idea. Send ___ the final version today. (they / them)
ejercicios.explica: Detrás del verbo va el objeto: send them.
Posesión de una persona: nombre + 's → Laura's desk.
Whose = de quién, y va pegado al sustantivo. Who's = who is.
Reflexivo de énfasis: herself (ella misma). Himself sería de un hombre.

ejercicios.es: La oficina de mis padres está en Chapinero.
ejercicios.en: My parents' office is in Chapinero.
ejercicios.explica: Plural en -s: solo apóstrofo (parents'). Parent's sería de uno solo.

ejercicios.frase: Is mine book on your desk?
correccion: Is my book on your desk?
ejercicios.explica: Delante de un sustantivo va my. Mine va solo: Is that book mine?

ejercicios.frase: The report of the client is ready.
ejercicios.explica: Con personas se usa 's, no «of»: the client's report.

ejercicios.frase: Your right, the deadline is Friday.
correccion: You're right, the deadline is Friday.
ejercicios.explica: You're = you are. Your es posesivo.

ejercicios.instruccion: Cambia «Laura» por el pronombre sujeto y «the report» por el pronombre objeto.
ejercicios.explica: Laura → she (sujeto); the report → it (objeto).

ejercicios.frase: This is the car of my boss.
ejercicios.explica: Persona + 's + cosa: my boss's car. El dueño va primero.

respuestas: Can you explain the brief to me?
Could you explain the brief to me?
ejercicios.explica: Explain + cosa + to + persona. Nunca «explain me».

ejercicios.es: Este escritorio es nuestro, y ese es de ellos.
respuestas: This desk is ours, and that one is theirs.
This desk is ours and that one is theirs.
This desk is ours, and that is theirs.
This desk is ours and that is theirs.
ejercicios.explica: Sin sustantivo: ours, theirs. Sin apóstrofo.

respuestas: We introduced ourselves to the client.
ejercicios.explica: Sujeto y objeto son la misma gente: ourselves.

ejercicios.texto: Whose idea was it, yours or hers?
respuestas: Whose idea was it, yours or hers?
ejercicios.explica: Whose pregunta de quién; yours y hers van solos, sin sustantivo y sin apóstrofo.

ejercicios.consigna: Presenta a tu equipo a un cliente nuevo: quién es cada uno, qué hace, y de quién es cada parte del proyecto (la estrategia, el diseño, la idea).
ejercicios.objetivo: adjetivos posesivos (our, her, his), pronombres posesivos (mine, his) y un reflexivo (ourselves)
ejercicios.ejemplo: This is Laura, our account director. Her team talks to you every week. Mike is our designer; the visual idea was his. The strategy is mine, but we wrote the deck ourselves, together.
ejercicios.explica: Our / her delante de sustantivo; his y mine solos; ourselves porque lo hicimos nosotros.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con la forma correcta del pronombre o posesivo. La pista en paréntesis es la traducción.
ejercicios.texto: My name is Andrés and I lead a creative team at Brava. Every Monday, {1} (nuestro) team has a short meeting. Laura, {2} (mi) account director, presents the week. The clients send {3} (nos) {4} (su, de ellos) feedback on Fridays, so Mondays are calm. Mike brings {5} (su, de él) laptop and shows the numbers. This routine isn't perfect, but it's {6} (nuestra, sin sustantivo), and it works. When something goes wrong, nobody blames anyone; we fix it {7} (nosotros mismos).
ejercicios.explica: Delante de sustantivo: our, my, their, his. Detrás del verbo: us. Sin sustantivo: ours. Nosotros mismos: ourselves.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta en cada desplegable: posesivo sin apóstrofo o contracción con apóstrofo.
ejercicios.texto: Hi team, {1} going to love this: the client approved the campaign. {2} the biggest project of the year, and {3} budget is bigger than we expected. {4} marketing director, Sarah, wants to meet on Thursday. {5} available at 10? Please bring {6} laptops and the final deck. Thanks! Camila
ejercicios.explica: Si puedes decir «are» o «is», lleva apóstrofo (you're, it's, who's). Si va delante de un sustantivo, es posesivo sin apóstrofo (its budget, their director, your laptops).

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el pronombre o posesivo correcto. La pista es la traducción.
ejercicios.texto: Last Saturday, my wife and I visited {1} (sus, de ella) parents in Chía. {2} (su, de ellos) house is small but beautiful. Her mother cooked for {3} (nosotros, objeto), and her father showed {4} (me, a mí) {5} (su, de él) new motorcycle. In the afternoon, the kids played by {6} (ellos mismos) in the garden while we talked. Family time is important to {7} (mí, objeto), and Saturdays like this one are the best part of the week.
ejercicios.explica: El posesivo concuerda con el dueño (her parents, their house, his motorcycle). Detrás de verbo o preposición: us, me. By themselves = solos.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el genitivo sajón ('s o s'), el posesivo o whose. La pista dice de quién es.
ejercicios.texto: At Brava, every account has an owner. The coffee brand is {1} (Laura, posesivo) account, and the bank is {2} (Mike, posesivo). The {3} (clients, plural, posesivo) feedback arrives on Fridays. {4} (Andrés, posesivo) job is to check that everyone's work is on time. Last week, the {5} (designers, plural, posesivo) files were late because {6} (su, de ellos) server crashed. {7} (de quién) fault was it? Nobody's. We fixed it together.
ejercicios.explica: Singular: nombre + 's (Laura's, Mike's). Plural en -s: solo apóstrofo (clients', designers'). Their delante de sustantivo. Whose = de quién.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el pronombre objeto, el reflexivo o el posesivo. La pista es la traducción.
ejercicios.texto: I usually go to the gym by {1} (yo mismo), but on Sundays my brother comes with {2} (mí, objeto). He pushes {3} (a sí mismo) hard; sometimes too hard. Last week he hurt {4} (a sí mismo) lifting weights. The trainer told {5} (le, a él) to rest, and now {6} (su, de él) shoulder is better. We enjoy {7} (nosotros mismos) there, and the gym is close to {8} (nuestro) apartment, so we have no excuses.
ejercicios.explica: Reflexivo cuando el sujeto y el objeto coinciden (he hurt himself, we enjoy ourselves); objeto cuando es otra persona (the trainer told him). By myself = solo.

ejercicios.texto: Hi Camila, thank you for the presentation yesterday. Our team really liked it, especially the second idea. It's simple, and its message is clear. My boss, Mr. Rojas, has two questions. First, whose idea was the music? He loved it and wants to meet the person himself. Second, can you send us the budget again? The file you sent me doesn't open on my laptop, but it works on Laura's. Also, please explain the timeline to me in a short call; I want to understand it before I present it to the board. Thanks again. The campaign is yours, and we're happy about it. Best, Sarah

preguntas.q: Who wants to meet the person who had the music idea?
In «its message is clear», its refers to…
Why does Sarah write «explain the timeline to me» and not «explain me»?
opciones: Because explain needs «to» before the person

ejercicios.explica: Its (posesivo) e it's (it is) conviven en el texto; explain lleva «to» delante de la persona; yours va solo, sin sustantivo.

ejercicios.texto: Every Sunday, my sister Laura and I have lunch at our parents' house in Suba. My mother cooks, and my father sets the table himself because he says nobody does it right. Laura always brings her dog, Tomás. He's small and noisy, but my parents love him. After lunch, my father shows us his garden. He's very proud of it: its tomatoes are the best in the neighborhood, or that's what he says. Laura and I wash the dishes ourselves so our mother can rest. Before we leave, my mom gives us food for the week. Hers is better than anything we cook at home, and she knows it.

preguntas.q: Why is it «our parents' house», with the apostrophe after the s?
opciones: Because parents is plural: the house of both parents

ejercicios.explica: Plural en -s: parents' house. Hers sustituye a «her food». Its (del jardín) sin apóstrofo. Himself y ourselves subrayan quién lo hizo.

ejercicios.texto: On Tuesday morning, Mike couldn't find his laptop. He looked everywhere in the office and asked everyone: Is this yours? Did you see mine? Laura checked her desk, and Andrés checked his, but nothing. Then Camila remembered something: the night before, Mike left the meeting room with the client's bag by mistake, and the client, Mr. Rojas, left with Mike's. Both bags were black. Camila called Mr. Rojas herself. He laughed and said: Your laptop is safe, and I need mine for a presentation at eleven! They met at a café halfway and exchanged the bags. Mike bought him a coffee to say sorry. Now Mike's bag has a big orange tag with his name on it.

preguntas.q: Whose bag did Mike take by mistake?
«Mike bought him a coffee» — him refers to…

ejercicios.explica: His y mine sustituyen al sustantivo (his desk, my laptop). Herself subraya que lo hizo Camila. Him es el objeto: otra persona, no el sujeto.

ejercicios.texto: Dear roommates, this is a note from Daniela, and it's not a happy one. Someone ate my yogurt again. It had my name on it: Daniela, in big letters. Whose idea was that? The fridge is ours, yes, but the food inside is not. Each shelf has its owner: the top one is mine, the middle one is yours, Kevin, and the bottom one is Sofía's. If you want something that isn't yours, ask. I always ask you. Also, the milk is everyone's, so if you finish it, buy a new one yourself. Thanks for understanding. Your hungry roommate, Daniela. P.S. Kevin, your mom called. She says you never answer her.

preguntas.q: «Each shelf has its owner» — why its and not it's?
opciones: Because it's a possessive: the owner of the shelf
Because it's short for it is

preguntas.q: «She says you never answer her» — her refers to…

ejercicios.explica: Ours, mine, yours van solos; Sofía's y everyone's son genitivos; its (posesivo) frente a it's (it is); her es objeto.

ejercicios.consigna: Describe a tu equipo de trabajo: quién hace qué, qué es de quién (el escritorio, el cliente, la idea) y algo que ustedes mismos hicieron.

requisitos.texto: Usa al menos dos adjetivos posesivos (my, your, his, her, our, their)
Usa un pronombre posesivo sin sustantivo (mine, yours, hers, ours, theirs)
Usa un genitivo sajón con nombre de persona + 's (Mike's laptop)

ejercicios.ejemplo: I lead a small team at Brava. Laura is our account director, and her desk is next to mine. Mike's laptop is always open because he checks the numbers himself. The coffee brand is Laura's client, but the idea for the campaign was ours: we built it ourselves in two weeks. Their feedback was great, and now my boss wants to show it to the whole agency.
ejercicios.explica: Adjetivo posesivo + sustantivo (her desk), pronombre posesivo solo (mine, ours), reflexivo (himself, ourselves) y genitivo 's para personas (Mike's laptop).

ejercicios.consigna: Cuenta un fin de semana con tu familia o amigos: de quién era la casa, quién cocinó para quién, qué hizo cada uno por sí mismo y algo tuyo que alguien usó.

requisitos.texto: Usa un pronombre objeto (me, him, her, us, them)
Usa un pronombre posesivo (mine, yours, hers, ours, theirs)
Usa un posesivo con nombre de persona + 's (Laura's house, my sister's car)

ejercicios.ejemplo: Last Saturday we went to my sister's house in Chía. Her husband cooked for us, and my mom brought her famous dessert. The kids played by themselves in the garden all afternoon. My nephew used my phone to take photos; the photos are his now, but the phone is still mine! At night, Laura's dog slept on my jacket, so now it has his hair all over it.
ejercicios.explica: Objeto detrás de verbo o preposición (for us), posesivo solo (mine, his), reflexivo (by themselves) y genitivo 's (my sister's house).

ejercicios.consigna: Escribe un correo corto a un cliente: confirma de quién es cada tarea (whose), pide que te expliquen algo (explain… to me), menciona algo del proyecto con its y aclara qué es suyo (yours).

requisitos.texto: Usa explain / send / show + algo + to me (nunca «explain me»)

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi Sarah, thanks for your call. Here is a quick summary. Whose task is the final budget? Ours: Laura is working on it and will send it to you on Thursday. The video is yours: your team records it, and we edit it. The campaign has a new name, and its logo is ready. One request: could you explain the new timeline to me in a short call tomorrow? I want to understand it before I share it with my team. Best, Andrés
ejercicios.explica: Explain + cosa + to me (no «explain me»); whose pregunta de quién; its es posesivo sin apóstrofo; yours va solo, sin sustantivo.
